recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is; no follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-7375 unless a future editorial pass revisits modifier-extension wording more broadly.
issue_request: FHIR-7375 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 technical correction for FHIR-core-extensibility section 1.16.0.2. It asked to change the malformed wording "Applications may also be able to ignore a modifier extension if that can know that this is safe..." to wording where applications know whether ignoring the modifier extension is safe.
initial_application: The Jira snapshot records Grahame Grieve's 2015-06-03 comment "svn revision 5385". The current git mirror does not expose a FHIR-7375-tagged commit, but git history shows b30002f3e69422b18d5a61bf0bb26122dc862638 introduced the malformed sentence in source/extensibility.html and bc32512f59b1d2696fbe6e89a6985b7840c4e924 later rewrote the passage to the corrected current form.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively maps the Extension type page to extensibility, so source/extensibility.html is in current build scope. The current page says applications might ignore a modifier extension if they know it is safe in their own context. Quoted Zulip and Confluence searches, plus a Confluence Jira-reference search, found no directly relevant community evidence or conflicting later decision for this typo.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the obsolete "if that can know" wording is absent from current source and the authoritative extensibility page already conveys the approved correction.
